tests/integration/hello_testkit.py -- Patch I01: the harness for the walking-skeleton tests.

One `Stack` joins the real pieces and fakes only what sits at a module boundary:

    real    codeagent.ws (S04) + router + run_handlers (S14) + emitter + hello (I01)

            the usage ledger (FakeLedger below), Redis (FakeRunRedis)

The device socket is served by uvicorn on 127.0.0.1 in a thread, so the genuine C04 client uses a
genuine TCP WebSocket (handshake, frames, abrupt connection loss). The client's source is
imported from the repo (m2c/src) because the backend's CI job does not pip-install m2c; its only
third-party dependency, `websockets`, is in the backend requirements.

Fake secrets are built at run time (gitleaks flags anything shaped like a key).

call 1 hits generate_text() and writes the registry, and call 2 doesn't
call generate_text() again and returns the identical brief.

is eo/panel.py's _get_or_write_role_prompt(), which every tab in the
Master Guide's B1 sector-2 list groups with the other agent-backed
integration tests since it's the one role-resolution path that makes its
own LLM call.

anymore either) -- this test covers the CURRENT contract:

dict ("Migration Part 27") confirms changelog_writer (and final_qa,

stays valid for the Panel to hire, but since it's not in

if a future migration silently breaks the generic_worker fallback for a

tests/test_inspector_diversity.py.

Bug caught by writing this test: the old script read `result['tier']`
off classify()'s return value. Per eo/inspector.py's own "Migration Part
12 §8.2/§8.4" comment, the output schema changed "tier" (int 0-3) to
"path" (string) -- classify()'s _validate() no longer puts a "tier" key
in its return dict at all. The old test would raise KeyError the moment
it ran against the current code instead of printing a diversity report,
which is exactly the kind of silent collection-time failure this sector
is meant to catch instead of finding out the hard way in production.

This also can't reasonably assert the SAME task always maps to the SAME
suggested_agents across a real model (that's what the old script
actually measured, by hitting a live LLM 5 times and eyeballing the
labels) -- with a mocked LLM we control the output directly, so instead

Real-Postgres checks for S06c (codeagent/run_manager.py).

The unit tests (tests/unit/test_codeagent_run_manager.py) use an in-memory twin of the run
store. This file runs the manager against the REAL `runs` table (migration 0014), so what
only Postgres can prove is proved here:

  * the sweep's one cross-account READ: the SQL of PgSweepStore, through the trusted
    internal path, returns only open, idle runs, in (updated_at, id) order, keyset-paged,
    and only ids and timestamps; a cursor with an acting user (not trusted) does not see
    other accounts' runs, so the sweep really does depend on that path;
  * expire_stale end to end: runs of two accounts are expired through the real conditional
    UPDATE, the trigger and the RLS policies (the write is made AS each run's owner);
  * the whole lifecycle -- start, pause, resume, end, cancel -- on real rows, and the
    cleanup rule (nothing left in Redis) after each ending;
  * a real race: eight threads ending one run at once -> exactly one winner.

Redis is the in-memory twin (tests/unit/buffer_testkit.py): this file is about Postgres.

what ends up in Redis, with no prefix to account for.

Real-Postgres checks for eo/workspace_code_files.py's version numbering.

The unit tests use a FakeCursor, so neither migration 0009's grants nor
the (workspace_id, file_path, version) primary key is ever exercised --
which is how "delete a file, re-create it, hit Save -> 500" shipped.

Skipped unless MINIME_TEST_DATABASE_URL is set. Point it at a scratch
database that already has migrations applied, connecting AS the app
role (minime_app), not postgres, so the grants are enforced:

    MINIME_TEST_DATABASE_URL="postgresql://minime_app@localhost/minime_test"         pytest tests/integration/test_workspace_code_files_pg.py

B01: the module-level guard below FAILS (it does not skip) when that URL
connects as a superuser, a BYPASSRLS role, or the owner of the code-file
tables, or when the database still lets minime_app UPDATE the version-history
table. In any of those cases every test here would pass without the grants
being exercised, and a reintroduced `UPDATE workspace_code_file_versions`
would go unnoticed. The workspace fixture also needs the test user to exist in
auth.users (README, "Real-database tests").
